claim.summary: For a finite-dimensional subspace U of a commutative ring R over a field and r(I)=dim U-dim(U cap I): r is antitone, r(I cap J)<=r(I)+r(J)-r(I+J), the stacked restriction to ideals I_1..I_M has rank r(cap I_a)<=sum r(I_a)-sum_{a>=2} r(I_a+I_b(a)) for any b(a)<a, and if each I_a contains one of K_1..K_C the joint rank is at most sum_c r(K_c). Increments r_U(I)-r_U(I+J) are monotone in U; for ideals generated by affine spans S_a,S_b in K[x_1..x_v] with 1 not in S_a+S_b, d_a=v-dim S_a and c=dim(S_a+S_b)-dim S_a, the increment for U inside degree<=k is at most c*binom(d_a+k-1,k-1). Elementary; no exactness hypothesis.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with its follow-up check, including the increment form. Submodularity is standard; ideals are generated by affine spans, so restriction is ordinary substitution.

claim.summary: In Braun's F2 one-level complete accuracy-3l old-affine setting over Q_{m,l}, n=2^l, if the input span of every proper block of rank>3l(k+1) contains one of C subspaces each of dimension>3l(k+1), and m ln(4C)<=k^2, k<=m, D>=6l+1, 2k(D+1)-1<=n, 4(k-1)<n, then there is no ordinary-PC refutation through degree D, whatever the number of blocks; it contains the published theorem (C<=M) and its polynomial-inventory corollary holds with C in place of the block count. At l=16 (k=302, D=107) a family with C=1 and more than 2^(771984*262063) proper blocks of rank 786529, with distinct incomparable restriction kernels, is excluded, while the published inventory condition fails at every admissible k.
claim.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with corrections and follow-up: kernel count, coverage by composition of restrictions, unchanged removal/separation/replay, eventual clause at the uniform-lemma k, the l=16 family and comparison. A gain only for families clustered by shared spans; generic families have C close to M.

claim.summary: Degreewise gluing: for U, W in the Boolean cube over any field, degree-d functions on U and W agreeing on U n W glue to a degree-d function on U u W iff I_d(U n W) = I_d(U) + I_d(W) iff dim F_d(UuW) - dim F_d(U) - dim F_d(W) + dim F_d(UnW) = 0 (always <= 0); this holds for all d <= D iff the graded Mayer-Vietoris sequence of graded function modules is exact through D. In characteristic p, gluing always succeeds after a shift delta = deg of a polynomial that is 0 on U and 1 on W minus U (k(p-1) for a k-form clause with F_p data), and for n sets in a chosen order I_d(n U_i) lies in sum_{i<n} I_{d+i delta}(U_i) + I_{d+(n-1)delta}(U_n).
claim.assessment: Working proof after a fresh-context review (hypotheses stated, n-set bound sharpened). Elementary; it identifies the Mayer-Vietoris route's exactness hypothesis, which fails on small boards.

claim.summary: For a finite-dimensional space S, subspace J, linear maps rho_a on S with stacked map rho and quotient q:S->S/J, the common kernel of the rho_a is not contained in J if and only if rank(rho,q)>rank rho; in particular when rank rho<dim S/J or sum of rank bounds r_a<dim S/J. In thm:certified-repair-composition with J=S cap J_D, its later stages use only a chosen w in the common kernel outside J_D, so the summed hypothesis may be replaced by any certificate of this exact criterion, with unchanged later costs. Certifying the criterion is a separate cost; on the marked Hermitian instance the summed and joint conditions fail (dim S/J=1) while the exact one holds.
